commands.evidence: 19 tests passed, 0 failures. Repository delivery and all write probes in the suite use disposable temporary fixtures.
Printed adapter usage and exited without runtime configuration.

checks.hard_link_sentinels: PASS: Independent temporary-repository probes hard-linked outside sentinels to .git/config and .git/refs/heads/sidequest-base. artifacts.freeze returned POLICY_DENIED and both sentinels remained byte-identical. A hard-linked progress file also returned POLICY_DENIED without changing its sentinel.
checks.config_atomic_replacement: PASS for an entry replacement race: a controlled fixture replaced .git/config with an outside hard link immediately before descriptor-relative os.replace; the outside sentinel remained unchanged and installed config had link count 1.
checks.configured_output_containment: PASS: An output_root outside artifact_roots and a symlink under artifact_roots pointing outside were each rejected with POLICY_DENIED; outside directories remained empty.
checks.state_and_delivery_hardlinks: PASS: Direct disposable-fixture probes rejected a pre-existing hard-linked delivery state file and a hard-linked destination file; sentinels stayed unchanged.
checks.approval_and_delivery_identity: PASS: B tests denied payload-only approval, stale/mismatched identity, changed destination, and reused delivery ID; one host-approved fixture delivery completed and an exact repeat reconciled to the same receipt.
checks.candidate_capture: PASS: B suite verified independent no-hardlink clone, unchanged source refs/files, add/edit/delete/rename/binary/mode capture, manifest/tree/patch hashes, and rejection of scope, traversal, symlink, oversize and credential-like inputs.
checks.same_uid_temporary_inode_race: LIMIT: In a disposable fixture, a controlled concurrent same-UID link to a newly opened candidate snapshot inode caused freeze to return POLICY_DENIED after the outside sentinel had already been overwritten with candidate-controlled bytes. The same class of race was demonstrated against the fresh .git config staging inode. This is not prevented by the adapter's post-write link-count checks.

findings.title: Concurrent same-UID access can link a fresh staging inode before its bytes are written
findings.reproduction: A deterministic temporary-fixture probe linked the new zero-length candidate snapshot inode to a sentinel outside every configured root immediately before os.write. The adapter later detected link count 2 and denied the freeze, but the sentinel already contained attacker-controlled candidate bytes. A similar probe against the fresh .git config staging inode replaced an outside sentinel with the fixed config contents before denial.
findings.impact: Static hard links, symlinked parents, and final-path redirection are rejected or atomically replaced. The adapter alone does not isolate a concurrent process with the same UID and write access to its configured roots. This remains a required sandbox/trusted-repository boundary; do not claim the B adapter is an OS sandbox or safe for hostile repositories.

limits: This PASS applies to B1's documented trusted-repository and active-worker-sandbox boundary. The adapter's path allowlists and descriptor-relative checks are not a separate UID/container boundary.

The same-UID concurrent temporary-file race is a known residual limitation, not evidence that the actual Codex sandbox can cross its configured write boundary. B2/host integration must enforce the mandated worker sandbox before execution.
All writes, approval checks and local delivery used disposable temporary fixtures. No real repository delivery, provider/model call, spending, authentication change, or source edit was performed.
